steps.text: The Year 1098
1:03 P.M. \ Overcast
Palace of Westhaleg, Londinium
Even before Londinium was a nomadic city, the Palace of Westhaleg stood here.
Its name was originally plain Westhaleg. The Draco royal family convened its ministers here in this palace, and used their beloved gold and ruby to decorate the outer walls.
Said decorations went up in flames during the Great Fire three hundred years ago. Still, the building's skeleton remained, and it bore witness to the first Aslan king's coronation.
Thereafter, Westhaleg formally became the Palace of Westhaleg, to commemorate the age of peace and prosperity founded by the Draco and Aslan kings in joint.
Twenty-six years ago, the last Aslan king was captured in the same place by Parliament's standing forces.
And now, this is no longer the building where the Victorian Parliament assembles.
Sat at the conference table is but one person, not Draco, nor Aslan, but Sarkaz.

steps.name: Voice on the Terminal
steps.text: ...still no sign of movement from the Duke of Gododdin... ever since the Viscount's life was attempted, our activity in the demesne has been greatly restricted...

steps.name: Voice on the Terminal
steps.text: ...lavish salons held every night at the Duke of Normandy's residence, but the flow of raw steel is extremely suspect, and all intelligence personnel have turned up empty-handed...

steps.name: Voice on the Terminal
steps.text: ...any sound from Dublinn is drowned out by the Duke of Wellington's high-speed battleships roaring. We've as of yet been unable to penetrate into the Iron Duke's duchy, but no other duke would be able to impede the veteran, without a doubt.

steps.name: Voice on the Terminal
steps.text: ...the Marquess and co. have finally given up on the Duke of Stafford's inheritance... the Duke of Caster admitted envoys and gifts on New Year's Eve...

steps.name: Voice on the Terminal
steps.text: ...activity from all dukes has been growing increasingly frequent since last winter. It may be a sign they're about to 'reach a conclusion.' Preparations for Londinium remain at the same pace as... hold for a moment, sorry.

steps.name: Voice on the Terminal
steps.text: What? You're sure... Leithanien? Three days ago? This is too slow! ...Yes, it looks like they've finally found results after their diplomatic peacemaking...

steps.name: Voice on the Terminal
steps.text: Er. New cipher's just been decoded. It's word from the frontline, General. Yes, I need to... notify you ASAP...

steps.name: Voice on the Terminal
steps.text: Three days ago, the Empresses' Voice grandiloquently left the Duke of Windermere's demesne... er...

steps.name: Voice on the Terminal
steps.text: (Gulps) We didn't discover contact between the two sides in time, but, just today...

steps.name: Voice on the Terminal
steps.text: A city... a fortress changed course, and is sailing straight for Londinium. The one that's been nearest us over the past two years... er...

steps.name: Voice on the Terminal
steps.text: It's pushing directly from Leithanien into the Victorian border, nearing the ravine. Er, yes, it's the Kurfürst's archenemy... Duke Windermere's army.

steps.name: Voice on the Terminal
steps.text: Duke Windermere announces internationally... this is to 'avoid Catastrophe.'
Silence once again hangs over the hall. But at this moment, with his eyes shut tight, Theresis sees the thick fog outside of Londinium.
Once it clears, the battle will come, right on schedule.
Footsteps break through Theresis's train of thought.
He is forced to open his eyes.
Ther...
Theresis.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: It's you.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Were you asleep?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: ...Perhaps.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The Victorian dukes are a cunning lot. They meticulously sift through every word of intel that flows into Londinium, making the Sarkaz lose their heads.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The advantage isn't ours in this gamble. Yet neither have we been at a disadvantage.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: The Military Commission's business is always endless. Such is our history's fragility... even a single comment on a piece of information awry would suffice to forever damn Kazdel.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But even now... now as we stand in Londinium, things have hardly changed much. You're still as weary as ever.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: No, one thing has changed.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You're here.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yes, I am.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The breadth of possibilities has crossed my mind, if you were to take my head. Perhaps you would make a much cleaner job of it than I.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You would never think that way yourself. That was a hypothetical put forth by Manfred.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I am always in need of some differing voices.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: What's on your mind now?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: A dream.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I saw us still in Londinium, yet unarmed.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Clouds enveloping this city, black stones growing everywhere, and the Sarkaz... the Sarkaz there in the way, between Catastrophe and the crowd.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Once the disaster lifted, Londinium's city gates were wide open to us, and the Victorians stood flanking the streets, cheering and welcoming us in.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: We entered this palace, and the one sat on the throne no longer feared the black stones that grew from us, and took our hands.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: He called the Sarkaz—

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: 'Friends.'

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: It sounds unfathomable.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: There was more.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I saw Vampire, Nachzehrer and Wendigo set foot together into reaches more northern than even Ursus, casting fragments of strange monsters back unto the frigid sky.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: And I saw Banshee and Damazti venture to parts more southern than even Iberia, walls against the ocean's dissent within the boundless water.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Countless Sarkaz giving their lives for this land—

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: And Aslan, Draco, Feline, Caprinae, Liberi... stood together with them.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Stood together?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Yes. The Sarkaz were no longer the nomads excluded. The land embraced us, and we had roots anew.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: This dream...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: This dream was not mine.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: This scenario all originates from what you once described to me... a future the Sarkaz could have.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I remember.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: But you told me, then, that my ideals were too distant, that it was not only our enemies who could never comprehend me, but neither could the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: A myriad years of grievances became our weapons one and all, and all imposed upon me.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You also told me that the flames of war within the Sarkaz would tear them apart before I led them to that future, that was more likely in all respects.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: But you begrudge giving up any possibility, even if it may be but a nascent spark.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: You've also said...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: That this world once was only the Sarkaz's. That the Ancients and Elders wrested our homeland from our forebears' hands.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Their souls in death still murmur the Sankta's betrayal, how the Royal Court withers like autumn leaves, how our bloodline is lost in howls of grief, how ridiculous the sinners are in forgetting history, and how Kazdel's ruins strew all across Terra.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: And then, they—cry out—

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: —'The Sarkaz have invaded our homeland.'

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: So better that the Sarkaz believe in the fight. The fight can herd our destinies together as one. Better that than...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: ...Peace.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: This isn't fair. To rule is a method of coexistence too.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Terra will perish by its own hand before it confronts those time-old questions.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: But our homeland would be more magnificent than the many of the Seaborn. Our hexcrafters would hold the northern menace at bay. Our knowledge, all-encompassing, would dispel Originium, end the Catastrophes...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Before all that, the Sarkaz must reach an answer.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: You're right... they must.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: This is a conversation we've had countless times, but now, you can hear their voices clearly. You can make real contact with their ancient souls' tendrils. So tell me, Theresa—

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: —Did this myriad of years of all the Teekaz souls that lived and breathed, and passed from life to the other shore in death—did they ever receive a momentary respite?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: I've already failed, Theresis.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Because you're a move behind.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Because at this moment, it is we that stand here.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Here...

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Londinium.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Tell me, Theresa.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: When you stand atop The Shard and look at this city, what is it you see?

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: That Victoria is a nation lush with ingenuity.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Without a doubt. In a few short centuries, they've built nomadic cities, withstood Catastrophe, even attempted to control the storm—

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Not to mention those knights of white steam. The valiance of those steel suits of armor that ventured into Kazdel, two hundred years ago, falls far short of that which I saw in the years to follow.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Ah... perhaps it's the fault of our unique blood, for granting so many of us lives far too long.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: So long that in the intervals between one war and the next, we lift our heads, only to realize that, excepting the Sarkaz, everyone is progressing on.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: No, it's nothing to do with the length of an individual's life.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: They have the opportunity to progress, simply because in the past they monopolized the freedom to choose between peace and war.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: Theresa, when I look at Londinium, I see the number of times this nation has gone wrong.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: The Victorians scorn how primitive the Sarkaz are, yet in essence they simply use the rules of the culture they founded to gild the greed and violence that runs in their deepest marrow.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: They tear at each other, incessantly. Ultimately, everything they've made will be ruined by their own hands.

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: That is why we could win this chance at freedom.

spans.text: is why we could win this chance at freedom.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Even if hope is still as remote?

steps.name: Theresis
steps.text: I won't give up on any possibility.

steps.name: Theresa
steps.text: Yes... in that regard, we've always been so alike.
The Year 1098
1:34 P.M. \ Overcast
Residence of the Duke of Cumberland, Auchterigg District of Londinium

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Amiya, Doctor, our Messenger has just sent back some key intel. The main Sarkaz forces are on their way back to the city right now. It's extremely likely this means they're about to wage war with the dukes' armies.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: But given previous intel, even if they do return to Londinium, the Sarkaz military won't be enough to directly contend with all the dukes.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: With the Sarkaz choosing to act now, they obviously believe they've grasped some key power that'll sway the situation for them.

options: The Shard.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: That skyscraper the Sarkaz occupied? We've learned there's weaponry concealed in the building, yes, but—will it sway things?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It will, Clovisia. Have your people ever taken note... of the storm above The Shard?

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Oh... those dark clouds seem highly unusual.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: According to the intel we've obtained, that's no normal storm at all. That's a Catastrophe The Shard is causing. Even if it isn't entirely the same as a true Catastrophe...

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: The Sarkaz want to cause a Catastrophe? They're still in Londinium themselves. What would they gain from destroying the city?

options: They plan to weaponize the storm.
What if they control where the Catastrophe lands?

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Hrmm.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We're not just conjecturing The Shard's purpose. This weapon... or this technology, rather, is exactly Rhodes Island's chief objective in entering Londinium.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Rhodes Island came for the clouds shrouding Londinium.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yes. It's not just a figure of speech.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: In the eventuality Theresis does activate The Shard, he'll lead the flames of war and the storm together, upon those he sees as the Sarkaz's enemies.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No Catastrophe Messenger could predict a man-made Catastrophe's course. No nomadic city could escape such a Catastrophe's assault.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Countless Sarkaz and Victorians will die in that battle, and it'll likely be even more tragic for those who survive. Most of them will become Infected.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Not to mention... The Shard isn't on the border, it's in Londinium, a nation's very capital...

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Which means...

options: Once the technology's complete, it'll reach anywhere on Terra.
We can only pray the tech hits further bottlenecks.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: The Sarkaz... will use Victoria's power to destroy her.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: If we reach that stage, then everything the Corps has done will be for naught.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Even if we could rescue people from a Catastrophe as Rhodes Island does... Londinium and our livelihood would be past any point of return.

spans.text: rescue people from a Catastrophe as Rhodes Island does... Londinium and our livelihood would be past any point of return.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Clovisia, Rhodes Island is greatly thankful to the Self-Salvation Corps. Without your help, we would've had no good way into Central Londinium.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But neither I nor the Doctor will lie to you. No matter how Rhodes Island plans to approach The Shard, the battles ahead will be brutal. Each more brutal than the last.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If we can't stop Theresis within the next few days, we'll be facing an all-out war, and the dukes will march with an eye to enter Londinium.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If the Corps chooses to wait for the dukes' armies...

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Amiya... we can't do that.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: I'm the daughter of a textiles merchant. Most of the fighters, in fact, are just ordinary civilians.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: We have workers, farmers, craftsmen, traders. Our backgrounds are a tapestry of millions, together under the one goal of driving the Sarkaz out of Londinium as soon as possible.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: That's why the Corps won't place all its hopes in the dukes. Otherwise, we'd never have been able to take a stand ourselves.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Our greatest fear, if it came to it, wouldn't even be the Sarkaz controlling The Shard. It'd be... the dukes, dropping any shred of thought for the ramifications.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: So... the Corps has no intent to suspend operations?

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: ...Correct.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: On the contrary, in fact. With war on the eve of breaking out, there are some things only the Self-Salvation Corps can do, here within Londinium.

options: Such as wrecking the Sarkaz defensive line from the rear.
Such as gaining as much possible intel on Sarkaz supply lines.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: We think alike, Doctor.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Should the dukes wage war, the Sarkaz will surely have preparations made to hold Londinium.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Being a steel fortress, Londinium is self-sufficient to an extent. However, the Sarkaz actions within the city have long since outstripped that load.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Still, unlike Londinium's previous masters, the Sarkaz don't get a drop of evident support from any of Victoria's other cities.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: In comparison, while the dukes do all act on their own liberties, they'll each have their own steady flow of supplies.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: A supply line... the Sarkaz do have some kind of hidden supply line, definitely.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Completing The Shard has been a multi-year undertaking. The idea they're relying solely on Londinium's own production is practically impossible.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It originates outside of the city, and its terminus... is in a Londinium munitions factory that builds weapons for the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Right. If we can locate this supply line...

options: Then the Corps could be decisive in the coming war.
We'll be able to delay the birth of a superweapon.
Commander Clovisia, cooperation is still our best choice.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: I'm afraid so, Doctor.

options: We need more intel on the munitions factory.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: The Corps has a fighter who knows Highbury in and out.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Doctor, you know him very well.

options: Feist?
The local friend who guided us.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Right. He's the most suited candidate for this mission.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: With some minor preparations, he'll lead everyone away from the Sarkaz's watch, and for the munitions factory.

options: We still need other, more concrete sources of info.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: ...The Defense Force's Command HQ.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: It's a tower, located at the border between Auchterigg and Highbury Boroughs, and it controls the info network for the entirety of Londinium's defense systems.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Given the supply line can penetrate Londinium, there must be records of it lying somewhere in the system.

options: I heard the majority of the Defense Forces...
There's traitors in the Defense's top brass, right?

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Their commander, Lettou, threw himself to the Sarkaz a few years back.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: It'd be pointless to try and win backing from a treasonist. If we plan to raid their command tower, we need some other way to seize system privileges.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Of course... method aside, there's the fact that our troops desperately need new armaments... The Sarkaz have placed their sights back on the city interior, and our supplies are stretched thin.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I'll think of some way to address supply needs. When it comes to keeping Londinium going day-to-day, there's still scarcely a Victorian trader who's fallen in line with the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Allerdale?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: However, in turn, there's a different matter that I need you all to help me with.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Clovisia, Rhodes Island has brought Artorius's relic back to Londinium.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Artorius? That's the surname the royal Draco's descendants took...

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Exactly. I've already checked with the Doctor and Amiya. It's the Artorius key, without a doubt.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: And that key... opens the way to the door of the Mausoleum of Kings. Which means we can retrieve the Realmblade, the 'Sighs of Kings.'

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Its significance goes beyond what any ordinary citizen would ever imagine. Trust me, please.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: It's not just some pretty piece of steel bestowed with symbolism. If we say The Shard is Londinium's great, incomplete ambition...

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Then the truth of the Victorian Realmblade and the Mausoleum of Kings—that would be Londinium's real ace in the sleeve.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: The Victorian Realmblade... isn't just symbolic?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Only a few nobles along with... Victoria's royal families knew about it. And I happen to be a Cumberland.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: I believe you. The Mausoleum of Kings is practically a thing of myth to us, but if a royal key can open the door to it...

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Amiya, how exactly did Rhodes Island even get this key...? Er, should I not have asked?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We won't conceal the key's history.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But it isn't Rhodes Island's. It bears tales upon tales that I was never a part of, and could never tell you.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: For Rhodes Island's time with it, though, I can tell you bit by bit if you're interested.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Thank you, Amiya.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: I'm just... floored, really. The legacy of Artorius... the truth of The Shard...

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: It's as if—Rhodes Island really has been preparing, for all these years now, to be here today in Londinium.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: But I won't delve any further for now. I won't make anyone else, either. It might lose us an important ally.

steps.name: Clovisia
steps.text: Phew... Amiya, Doctor, do you have anything else you want to tell me?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: There is... one other thing, in fact.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Clovisia, about my background. I'd like to have a chat with you.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...The flowers. Doctor, look at these flowers.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: They're growing.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's amazing, a place like this, in the middle of Londinium, in a Sarkaz-occupied city...

options: For the Sarkaz, not letting nobles go is a net plus...
But it can't be the same for those around Miss Allerdale...

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: You're both quite right, Doctor, Miss Amiya.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Despite it being slightly neglected these past years, the Duke of Cumberland's manor is still Londinium's most iconic building.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I've not much recollection of my home out in the duchy. My childhood memories mostly tie back to here.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Nobody would ever truly leave this place to rot, would they?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Miss Allerdale!

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: The fact she went to lay everything bare to Miss Clovisia, while it turns out your crew were already wise to Her Highness's identity... I didn't expect that, I'll confess.

options: Siege is a vital operator of ours.
Vina and I do get along real well.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Well, well... that reply of yours surprises me even more. Rhodes Island knew who Her Highness was... yet have been willing to treat her as Vina, leader of the Glasgow Gang.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Give Clovisia and Vina some more time. The Corps have their disagreements when it comes to nobles, you know, and Her Highness is... going to have a lot to say.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I'm sure you have questions for me, too, mysterious little bunny? I'd like to jibber-jabber a little with the enigmatic Rhodes Island myself, before it's time to mingle with the merchants.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Miss Allerdale... is this residence truly secure?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Hm. Rational question.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: The Sarkaz naturally have their motive for not flushing out the nobles in Central. Londinium's a massive city. There's much too much for them to mind.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: But... we've paid a tremendous price to sit in the middle of a war unscathed, Miss Amiya. Dignity, or what have you, is the least valuable part of it.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Given the chance, I'll explain to Rhodes Island in detail. But the Sarkaz informants surveilling this manor are under our control, and for now, I ask you trust me.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: They haven't realized we've infiltrated them. They're wrong to believe Londinium's city nobles lost their every weapon after being isolated. Their mistake.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: You still have some way to counter Sarkaz surveillance?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Provisionally...

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Hm, no. If Her Highness has decided to be forthright with the Corps, then it's not my place to be covering up either.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: For the sake of a smooth partnership, I can explicitly guarantee to you all that, even now, the Cumberland residence has people who can establish extracity contact.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But the Sarkaz aren't fools. They're well-versed in war.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Indeed. But like I told you, Londinium's a massive city. They don't have enough people, they're all on their own, and that serves us opportunities.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...Correct.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Seems I haven't satisfied you much with my response?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No. Miss Allerdale. I just...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Worry your burden's too heavy.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: If there really is some way for Victoria to keep control of Londinium, as it is now...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No... I believe they can.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But if they truly can, if they ultimately can, then what is it that they've been doing in practice all these years, that they've been having you do?
Allerdale's face clearly twists for an instant.
That flash of emotion is immeasurably magnified in Amiya's eyes. It's no simple resentment, nor wariness, nor panic.
It's grief.
A grief so familiar it hurts.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I apologize, Miss Allerdale... I know I've offended you.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Clovisia was right. We don't need to pry into each other. It could very well strain our progress instead, with this complex state of affairs.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But, if possible...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Please don't stifle yourself. We've seen the consequences of that time and again.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Miss Allerdale? I—I'm being too heavy-handed, aren't I...

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: No. Rhodes Island just keeps on astonishing me... It seems I was judging you by your cover.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: I never did imagine you'd be this sort of leader. You must be at least a decade younger than me, but the look in your eyes is a very real thing.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Not to mention... heh, well, you've seen right through me. Considering you even cracked the secret of The Shard ahead of Clovisia and I, and brought the Red Dragon's key with you...

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Honestly, if Her Highness hadn't vouched for you, I might just've been even warier of Rhodes Island than the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: It's true, Londinium... no, the Sarkaz, to us, have more significance still.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: That's why we're here.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Well, then. You're here. What are you fighting for?

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Her Highness gave me a simple synopsis of Rhodes Island. You seem to be all sorts of bound up with the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: But according to what I've heard, Rhodes Island has, and has always, worked for the sake of the 'Infected.'

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We do.

steps.name: Allerdale
steps.text: Then the two of you must have plenty more going on in your heads right now, leader and commander of Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: As you say, there's a great deal of people and affairs in Londinium that we have inseparable ties to.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm only speaking personally... and for the Doctor too, when I say that the truth and the past may be enough impetus on their own at this point for us to act.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But we've already been through so much. It's long stopped us from frivolously viewing these struggles and calamities, or placing our individual feelings above the greater problem.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: That's why we're here to curb a war that would devastate the land, and to dissipate the ground zero of Victoria's woes.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: To prevent the extinction of a race. To find the lifeline that by all rights we have the methods to seek.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: To help the Infected, the workers, and even the Sarkaz that have been desolated.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We're here to help 'people,' Miss Allerdale. Every single person with life. Every single person with the right to live.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Only in the end that the majority can accept... do the truths of the past have any significance.
Amiya finishes her speech with resolution.
In Allerdale's clear look of surprise, Amiya can't help but seek her heart.

a.text: She's spoken her most genuine, sincere mind. Of that, there is no doubt.
The operators that work alongside her must surely be filled with the same staunch conviction. Dr. Kal'tsit stands ever more alone, carrying the weight of ideals.
So this ideal's origin, this strong flame of conviction that drives Rhodes Island to move in such colossal risk, to rush headlong into this political maelstrom—who lit it?

steps.text: And what if—
—this answer of hers remains incapable of solving these pressing issues?
